citations: "The West-dealer annual rows have unique `source_event_id` values, and the import log reports no duplicate source events."
"The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "transaction clustering is an operational batching artifact rather than commercial manipulation."
"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates; the May rows have effective dates from 1–28 May and post on 31 May."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "leaving revenue-recognition policy and entitlement activation as the two explicit open unknowns."
"If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The single next action is one read-only verification query comparing the West-dealer trend by `posted_at` and `effective_event_date`, alongside a small entitlement sample."
"It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no source record, makes no posting change, and its output can be discarded."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Keep restatement on hold pending the result."
"otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Cross-checking the raw files against operational claims confirms that the 17-row 31-May cluster is an expected month-end batch ... with ... no evidence of billing manipulation." The operational email corroborates the batching mechanism but does not establish that every row is genuine or rule out manipulation by itself.

"This inference firmly resolves data-pipeline and fraud hypotheses." Import acceptance, unique source IDs, and cash reconciliation rule out duplicate-source and certain import failures, but do not fully exclude downstream reporting defects, provisioning failures, or all forms of manipulation.

"No revenue restatement, billing reversal, or pipeline remediation is warranted." Entitlement activation and the governing reporting clock remain unverified, so this should be conditional rather than stated categorically.

"The two May dealer files accepted every received row ... across all 90 West-dealer annual renewals." The cited import-log fields support acceptance and reconciliation, but the submission does not provide the actual row-level join or query demonstrating that those files cover exactly all 90 rows.

"The 90 West-dealer annual rows have effective dates in the same calendar month as their posting dates." This is potentially misleading for the month-end anomaly: the key finding is that event dates span the month while posting is concentrated at month-end, and the claim needs precise row-level qualification.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled entitlement-activation failure and reporting-policy ambiguity, but did not fully test them before recommending closure. The strongest missed alternative is that the dealer import can be cash-reconciled and duplicate-free while still producing a downstream analytics or entitlement-provisioning defect; acceptance and reconciliation alone do not exclude those mechanisms.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform and report the promised entitlement and event-time checks before making the categorical no-escalation conclusion, with a reproducible row-level join showing all 90 West renewals, unique source events, cash reconciliation, activation outcomes, and downstream use of `effective_event_date`.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South NO_SIGNAL tickets fell from 51 in May to 28 in June, but service-event data still records 10 May events affecting 9,409 accounts and 8 June events affecting 7,045 accounts."
"Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The drop in logged South complaints is substantially confounded by changed session-filtering rules and pre-authentication drop-offs that never reach CareDesk."
"The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."
"I cannot resolve what follows an `authenticate` ERROR/ABANDONED session... without tracing a sample and obtaining the written metric definition."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Do not expand NovaIVR nationally on current evidence."
"Keep the rollout decision on hold pending the result."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "underlying network service events remained steady across May and June" is stronger than the cited figures support: events declined from 10 to 8 and affected accounts from 9,409 to 7,045, with no normalization or pre-pilot comparison shown.
"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" is not established by authentication abandonment alone; the submission itself acknowledges that downstream recovery and customer outcomes are unknown.

"Telemetry in `service_events.csv` confirms ongoing customer impact" overstates what service-event counts establish: they show material service events and exposure, not necessarily complaint experience or individual customer harm.

The claim that the drop was caused by "channel filtering" is plausible and supported by the exclusion rule, but the submission does not demonstrate that the excluded sessions represented failed complaint journeys rather than benign abandonment or successful alternative resolution.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—genuine self-service deflection—by identifying balance-check and pack-information stages and preserving that possibility. It missed a fuller alternative in which some authentication abandonment reflects voluntary exit, successful resolution through another path, or non-complaint intent; abandonment is not itself evidence of dissatisfaction. It also treated service-event persistence as evidence of customer impact without testing the relationship between events and complaint journeys.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end journey validation, not only a repeat-contact query: link sampled NOVA sessions—including authentication ERROR/ABANDONED sessions—to subsequent contacts and outcomes, and listen to a representative sample of calls. This would test whether missing case creation reflects suppressed complaints, benign abandonment, or successful recovery.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites specific CSV rows and fields for the central observations: "impact_mw=0" and "cleared=yes" for all four records, plus event, severity, duration_min, timestamp_local, and inverter_id.
The claims about dates, inverter IDs, durations, and constant fields are explicitly tied to `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, rather than presented as unsupported summary conclusions.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It cross-checks severity and event labels against duration, cleared status, impact_mw, recurrence, and inverter distribution: "Labels alone do not establish failure."
It tests a plausible innocent explanation—limited or filtered export—by noting "no plant-wide denominator or extraction filter" and recommending an unfiltered read-only query.
The analysis is strong within the supplied extract, but it does not truly triangulate independent operational channels beyond fields in the same event file.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It explicitly limits the conclusion to "this 4-row extract" and says completeness must be confirmed before treating it as representative.
It distinguishes a data-scope check from evidence of equipment breakdown and states that "constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units."
It identifies decision-changing evidence: recurrence, open faults, critical severity, or nonzero generation impact.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation—"Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check"—is proportionate to four short, cleared, zero-impact events.
The proposed read-only export query for 27 May–4 June without status filters is safe, reversible, and directly discriminates between a complete benign extract and a filtered or incomplete one.
The conditional follow-up—re-evaluate if open faults or nonzero-impact events appear—preserves an appropriate operational response without inventing a plant problem.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: "Do not escalate on this 4-row extract" accurately reflects the visible evidence and is appropriately scoped rather than asserting that the plant is definitively healthy.
The conclusion matches the key dynamics: zero MW impact, short durations, cleared events, and a communications warning that does not by itself establish equipment failure.
The submission stops after a narrowly targeted completeness check instead of searching for an unsupported story.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase "routine, cleared operational events" is somewhat broader than the extract proves; the records are cleared and short, but "routine" is an interpretation.
"Self-cleared" is not directly established by a `cleared=yes` field unless that field's semantics are known; "cleared" would be more precise.

"If these are the only four records, close the review" is reasonable for this event-review question but still depends on the proposed export being confirmed complete and on there being no separate operational evidence outside the file.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 7-minute `COMM_LINK_WARN` could reflect a transient communications or telemetry issue rather than inverter damage. Alternatively, the four-row extract could be incomplete or filtered; that is the main evidence-based alternative and is appropriately handled with the proposed unfiltered export check.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State explicitly that `cleared=yes` does not necessarily prove automatic recovery, and verify the export's time range, timezone, status filters, and row-count/completeness metadata in the read-only query.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "On 29 May, 84 blocks retain qca_base and 12 are pilot_revision" with specified fields from dispatch_blocks.csv.
"The headline arithmetic is reproducible" using the two daily dsm_penalty_rs totals.
The submission separately cites DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf for tariff and settlement limitations.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: It explicitly notices that the headline compares two dates and constructs a same-day modeled comparison using base_schedule_mw versus submitted_schedule_mw on 29 May.
It tests innocent explanations and limitations including daily baseline variability, selection and timing, incomplete commercial settlement, and differing deviation metrics.
It distinguishes the observed pilot-day result from causal attribution: "neither estimate establishes a general causal effect."

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The evidence table assigns different confidence levels, including "High for arithmetic; Medium for causal interpretation."
It states that the 17.6% result is "descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof."
It identifies decision-changing unknowns involving pre-outcome selection, immutable timestamps, replication, and net value.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to hold expansion and run a "read-only shadow calculation" preserves operational constraints and avoids changing submitted schedules or plant control.
The proposed prospective validation captures immutable timestamps, uses pre-registered matched high-wind events, and includes net commercial settlement rather than DSM penalties alone.
The action is explicitly reversible and linked to discriminating evidence.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion keeps the smaller same-day benefit rather than dismissing the pilot: "about 17.6% lower" on 29 May.
It accurately scopes 31.6% as a descriptive cross-day difference and rejects treating it as a controlled causal estimate.
"Insufficient evidence that the AI pilot caused a 31.6% improvement" is well aligned with the supplied causal limitation.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the read-only shadow calculation is "cheap" and that its output "can be discarded" is an operational assumption rather than something demonstrated by the cited files, though it is not material to the analytical conclusion.

The phrase "stronger same-day modeled estimate" could be read as implying greater evidentiary strength; the submission appropriately limits it to a one-day modeled counterfactual, so this is at most a minor wording risk.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a real, directionally favorable reduction on 29 May, but the improvement could reflect the particular day's conditions, schedule selection, or model assumptions rather than the pilot itself. The evidence supports retaining that possibility while withholding causal attribution and expansion.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the 17.6% same-day calculation fully auditable by providing the exact banded-penalty formula, per-block base-versus-submitted calculations, and immutable pre-submission timestamps; then replicate that pre-specified comparison across multiple pilot days.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix confirms 90211000 is valid for Switzerland" is slightly stronger than the cited matrix evidence if the matrix is not itself legally authoritative; the submission appropriately qualifies this by requiring Tares confirmation.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is an absence-of-evidence assertion and would be stronger if tied to an explicit packet-wide search scope.
"CHF 126,900 total closes it" is not fully explained as a decision criterion and appears contingent on a broker calculation that is not yet supplied.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: 90211090 could still be the legally applicable Swiss code on 2025-11-04 because the cited Swiss matrix row begins on 2025-01-01 and may not establish the effective Tares or ruling position for the declaration date. That alternative is correctly retained for verification rather than treated as proof of broker non-compliance.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State explicitly that the Swiss Matrix is a reference signal rather than legal authority, and provide the exact effective-date Tares or ruling record needed to validate 90211000 for 2025-11-04.

"‘Commercial manufacturing country in commercial_invoice.pdf disproves preference’: rejected because manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preferential origin"
"‘The shipment should be flagged for fraud’: rejected because absence of a supplier declaration... represents unverified documentation, not intentional misdeclaration."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The claim is unsupported by packet evidence, but not disproved."
"valid supplier declarations may exist in procurement archives."
"A valid document would resolve the gap; no document would support a control correction, but still not prove fraud."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv` or procurement folders... is the required proof."
"Whether evidence exists outside the incomplete register | Targeted search of Procurement's category folder"

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"Request the active supplier declaration and originating rule from Procurement."
"without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is too categorical: a supplier declaration may be important evidence, but the submission does not establish that this exact document type and system linkage are legally required in every applicable route.

"My inference is that this represents an evidence-tracking gap rather than commercial misrepresentation" goes beyond the evidence if read as a positive finding; the records show missing support and do not resolve whether the issue is a control gap, an unlocated document, or an incorrect claim.

"SUP-03/05/06 plus valid proof could support preference" is conditional but still omits confirmation that those suppliers actually supplied this shipment and that the relevant preferential-origin rule is satisfied.

"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral)" does not explain the legal or computational basis for the duty treatment and could conflate withholding preference with establishing a final duty outcome.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been supplied by SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, with a valid declaration stored outside the packet or register; alternatively, the shipment may have been supplied through SUP-02 after its recorded validity period or by a non-preferential supplier. The present evidence therefore supports an unresolved documentation and linkage issue, not either confirmed preference or fraud.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the applicable proof and origin rule precisely, then reconcile the shipment to its actual supplier and procurement record before characterizing the claim as non-preferential or deciding the resulting duty treatment.

"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches in live QCore and CertVault before building a dashboard."
"Immediate dashboard release is safe" is rejected because of missing evidence timestamps, right-censoring, and snapshot defaults.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed": rejected because 185 of 262 release timestamps ... are defaulted to 02:10:00 snapshot boundaries.
"Discard the extract as corrupt": rejected because duration arithmetic is valid and monotonic.
"Whether 02:10 is a real disposition time or extract default" is explicitly left open for live-record testing.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows"
"evidence_available_ts or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches"
"Next Verification Step: Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches in live QCore and CertVault"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 02:10:00 "represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" is stronger than the available evidence supports; the concentration and snapshot-time match establish a serious artifact hypothesis, but live audit is still needed to distinguish defaulting from genuine releases at that time.

The claim that excluding default-timestamp rows gives an "evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is not traceable to the described extract because evidence_available_ts is explicitly missing; it should be labeled as a different proxy or removed.

The claim that the 42 HOLD rows are "likely to become the slowest observations" is plausible but not demonstrated, especially because the HOLD rows are from a later receipt cohort than completed rows.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps could be genuine release or disposition times for a nightly operating process rather than purely defaulted interface commits, while the apparent performance difference could also reflect the later receipt dates of the open HOLD cohort. Live audit-log timestamps and a coherent point-in-time reconciliation across QCore, LabTrack, and CertVault would discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Remove or relabel the unsupported "evidence-to-release median of 8.4 hours" and explicitly separate measured receipt-to-release or lab-complete-to-release proxies from the unavailable SOP evidence-to-release KPI; then use the proposed 5–10-row live audit to validate timestamp semantics before calculating any compliance metric.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: “Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records” for the 11 blank-part-number requests.
“Live local CMMS reservation and availability query” for current free stock.
“Receiving engineer and qualification approval” for revision substitutions.
“Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search” to determine whether a pilot adds value.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately” overstates what an identity match establishes: the submission itself identifies reservation, revision, qualification, UOM, and stale-stock constraints that can still prevent transfer.

The classification of eight requests as “Actionable now” is stronger than the evidence supports because the global MaintStar snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with 24 July; current confirmation is still required.
“The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests” is a candidate-value estimate, not yet an actionable realized saving, given the stale availability data and required operational approvals.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The evidence supports exact MPN matching as a strong candidate-generation baseline and may show that semantic search adds limited value for populated requests, but semantic search could still materially improve recall for the 11 blank-MPN requests. The best conclusion is therefore a controlled comparison or pilot, not a definitive dismissal of semantic search.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Separate candidate value from actionable value explicitly: relabel the eight “actionable now” items as provisionally eligible candidates, run a current local-CMMS reservation/availability check plus engineering qualification check, and report the conversion rate from exact-match candidates to approved transfers before claiming savings.
